Faith and Worship

It is important for us to develop the children’s understanding of our core values by demonstrating them ourselves and showing our children how we can live and develop moral and spiritual awareness.
We explore the meanings of the core values and their significance through daily acts of worship. The gifts of Generosity, Compassion, Courage, Forgiveness, Friendship, Respect, Thankfulness, Trust, Perseverance, Justice, Service and Truthfulness are the key values we want our children to understand and develop before they leave primary school. Daily Worship
With Love & Faith, We Aspire & Achieve.
Jesus said: I have come so you may have life, life in all its fullness. John 10:10
Each day there is a daily act of worship, which is inclusive and invitational - this is lead by the children who open and close the worship.
Each act of worship has a different story and related activities.
We start each week with a story, this could be a bible story, a contemporary story or a story from another faith as well as Christian and other faith festivals. This could include world and localised events. From these stories worship activities are planned by teachers using the ‘Telling the story, making sense, making connections and understanding the impact’ framework. These activities might be discussion based, or children completing a specific activity. These are recorded in our Worship Floor books as well as being part of our reflection spaces.
There are refection areas in each classroom where children are given the opportunity to reflect on Collective Worship, RE teaching, spiritual development or just to take the time to think in a quite space.

Prayer Spaces
With Love & Faith, We Aspire & Achieve.Jesus said: I have come so you may have life, life in all its fullness. John 10:10
Prayer spaces help children to reflect and pray, each classroom has a dedicated area for prayer and reflection.
Prayer spaces enable children, of all faiths and none, to explore life’s questions, spirituality and faith in a safe, creative and interactive way.
A prayer space is an area that is used to encourage personal reflection using a range of creative activities. This could include issues such as forgiveness, injustice, thankfulness, peace, big questions, identity and stillness.
Most recently, the children completed the Mountain activity. This reflects our value of courage as life's journey is like climbing a mountain and we achieved this in 3 stages. Starting at the bottom with their hopes and dreams, then thinking of a particular challenge they are facing and how God could help them to achieve this. Finally, when they reach the top they can celebrate their achievements - no matter how small!

With Love & Faith, We Aspire & Achieve.
Jesus said: I have come so you may have life, life in all its fullness. John 10:10
Every year the school celebrates St Matthew’s saint’s day on the 21st September. This gives the school the opportunity to reflect on the life of St Matthew: the importance of his story and how we can use this to support and develop our understanding of being a Christian. We also read stories from his gospels as well as thinking about the school’s core values.
This year we thought about our spiritual journey and how we can use reflection spaces in our classroom to help with this.
We also began to develop Prayer Spaces within the school.

British Values
At St-Matthew’s we agree with the Department for Education’s five part definition of British Values:
We believe it is incredibly important that these British Values permeate through every school in the country. At St-Matthew’s C of E Primary school children encounter these values throughout our everyday school life, especially through our promotion of the Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural aspects. Our Statutory Inspection of Anglican and Methodist Schools (SIAMS) report (2015) recognised us as a ‘Good’ Church of England School. This means that our school is distinctively and recognisably a Christian institution. We believe that our Christian identity plays an important role in upholding British Values within our school community. Our values and school vision correlates closely with the Department of Education’s British Values. Below is a snap shot of how we promote these values in our school community:
Democracy
The rule of law
Individual liberty
Mutual respect
Democracy
Pupil voice plays a big part of life at St-Matthew’s C of E Primary School. All pupils are given the chance to be a school council representative and they play a strong role in school improvement. Pupils have input in their learning and what they would like to learn which promotes pupil voice. For example, the pupils are involved in choosing texts, topics and themes. Pupil questionnaires, conferences and democratic voting are also conducted throughout the year. We feel that these opportunities to shape their school will sow the seeds for a more sophisticated understanding of democracy in the future.
The Rule of Law
We want our pupils to understand that whether these laws govern the class, the school, the neighbourhood or the country, they are set for good reasons and should be followed. The understanding of our school rules is consistently reinforced in corridors and classrooms, through collective worship and in our curriculum. The involvement of our pupils in the creation of the class rules helps them to understand the reasons behind rules and the consequences if these rules are broken. Throughout the year we welcome visits from members of the wider community including police, church, hospitals, the fire brigade and many more. We believe that clear explanations and real life stories emphasise the importance of the Rule of Law for our pupils.
Individual Liberty
We focus heavily on creating a positive culture in our school, so children are in a safe environment where choices and freedoms are encouraged. Our positive behaviour policy encourages pupils to make individual choices. Through our E-Safety, countryside skills and PSHE sessions, we educate children on their rights and personal freedoms as well as supporting them in recognising how to exercise these freedoms safely. We offer a range of clubs which pupils have the freedom to choose from, based on their interests. At St-matthew’s we believe that valuing choice and freedom in daily school life will foster a value for individual liberty as the children embark upon their adult lives
Mutual Respect
Our school vision states: ‘With love and faith, we aspire and achieve’
Respect and love towards others is one of our core values and therefore it plays an important role in our daily life. Mutual respect is promoted daily through the school rules and using our collective worship time. Our ‘Playground champions’ programme, ‘reading buddy’ system and links with a local care home all help to support the children’s respect of others. Our link with a School in the Western Province of Kenya also gives the pupils a wider sense of mutual respect. Mutual respect is at the core of our school life.
Tolerance of those of different faiths and beliefs:
Whilst we are a Church of England School, we offer a culturally rich and diverse curriculum in which all major religions are studied and respected. Parents and leaders of different faiths are welcomed to the school to share their beliefs. At St-Matthew’s we strongly believe that tolerance is gained through knowledge and understanding. Through our curriculum and the routines of our daily school life, we strive to demonstrate tolerance and help children to become knowledgeable and understanding citizens who can build a better Britain for the future.

Head Teacher’s Welcome
Dear Parents and Carers
Welcome to St Matthew’s Primary School. I hope you take the time to read all about the things going on in our school and realise, like we do, that St Matthew’s is a brilliant school to send your children to. The best way to really get to know us is to come and visit, and see all the amazing learning that is going on. In the meantime, here’s a little bit about how we work and why we are the right choice for you for your child.
With Love & Faith We Aspire & Achieve
Jesus said: I have come so you may have life, life in all its fullness: John 10:10
At the heart of St Matthew’s School is our community, our family, where we all show kindness and compassion to all. In the hearts of our children are love, respect, resilience and perseverance, we nurture each other so we can learn and flourish together, living life in all its fullness.
As you can see, our vision is to support your child to flourish and thrive. We know that, for our children and school community to live life in all its fullness, we need to be the wider family, to nurture and support all in the St Matthew’s family, to raise aspirations so all can fully embrace their successful futures. We want all in our school community to live life in all its fullness.
Love: we want our children, families and staff to feel loved and cared for, and to feel compassion and kindness towards others. At the heart of St Matthew’s is our nurturing approach where we want all our stakeholders to feel a part of our St Matthew’s family; where everyone feels valued and shows care for themselves, others and their environment. Being a part of the St Matthew’s family is important to our children, staff and wider community. This reflects the close-knit community of Cainscross where many families have continued to live and work in the same area for generations. Family brings us closer together and supports us all to show consideration and compassion for each other.
Faith: St Matthew’s is fully inclusive to those with a Christian faith, different faith and for those of no faith. We have faith in our self and others, to help us all succeed. St Matthew’s church continues to be a close part of who we are. Local leaders from the Church are regular visitors to school, leading Collective Worship and working in school. Collective worship helps our children to reflect on big questions and learn how those with faith have overcome challenges in their lives. Staff and governors have positive interactions so that children feel safe and well cared for. Our 7-values are linked to scripture and Bible stories so children can reflect on positive behaviours through the teachings of Jesus. Leaders have faith in all staff to realise their potential and flourish.
Aspire: we have aspirational goals for our children and staff. Our curriculum is based on key drivers to raise children’s horizons. We want our children to look beyond the immediate locality, and to learn about the wider world, learning about and from other cultures and faiths, showing respect for all. Literature and quality books are a key part of our curriculum delivery so that children receive a rich, diverse language as part of their daily educational diet. We want our children to persevere and stick at tasks, achieving a sense of fulfilment. We build resilience in our children so they do not give up as the going gets tough, but they keep going until the job is done.
Achieve: the core subjects of reading, writing and maths are strong across the school. Children achieve well. Our challenging curriculum matches the aspirations of the National Curriculum. We look at developing the whole child through a particular focus on sport and drama so that our children can go on and be the best they can be, and be ready for the next stage of their education. We want our children, families and staff to learn and flourish, and live life in all its fullness.
I hope you come and visit the school and see all the amazing things that happens when you come to be a part of the St Matthew’s family. We look forward to seeing you at school soon

Information for Parents
Dropping your child off at school
As a general rule children should not arrive at school before 8:30am when there will be members of staff on duty in both the junior and infant playgrounds. Once a child has arrived, they must not leave the school again without permission. Children should go straight to the playground and should only go to their classroom if asked to by a teacher, or have a genuine reason for doing so. Should it be a wet day, children will be directed by a teacher straight to their classrooms.
Collecting your child from school
At the end of the school day please wait for Junior children by the playground gates. The children will be brought to the gate by their teachers. The infant children can be collected from their teachers at the infant gate. Children will only be released to known parents or carers. If a parent wishes their child to go home with another adult, or independently, they must inform the school office or teacher beforehand.
Morning break
Children can bring a snack to school for this break. We ask that children only bring healthy foods (such as fruit or vegetables). Please make sure that it can be eaten easily whilst the children are in the playground. The children are also encouraged to have a drink at break time. They can have either water, a drink brought from home, or cartons of milk can be purchased. Please see the School Secretary for a form to order milk. Children entitled to free school meals are also entitled to free school milk.
Parent’s Evenings
It is important to keep up with your child’s progress. With this in mind parent’s evenings are held in the Autumn and Spring terms and a written report provided in the Summer term. If your child’s teacher has any particular concerns, they will arrange a meeting with you. If you have any worries about your child’s progress, please talk to your child’s teacher at the end of the school day or speak to the school office so that a mutually convenient meeting time can be arranged.
Parent’s at the School Gate
Many friendships develop at the school gate. You will be able to share school related concerns with more experienced parents and ease some worries you may have. However, sometimes what is said may not be true, or the full information, and consequently may make you more anxious. If you have any concerns, always talk to the class teacher to avoid being misinformed.

English Curriculum
Writing
At St Matthew's, we believe that writing is the window for children to show and share their ideas from across the curriculum and from their growing understanding of their wider world.
To support this, we use a clear systematic approach to the teaching of writing. We have worked closely with other DGAT schools to develop an approach which ensures that we develop exciting and engaging learning experiences for our children so they can develop their skills to be excellent writers and authors.
Writing is often centred around broad themes linked to class topics to excite and engage the children. All classes use a two weekly approach to writing with one week focusing on key skills and knowledge while the second week embeds these using different genres.
Role play, discussion and debate is often used to enrich the writing experience. Teachers regularly model writing to demonstrate the approaches for different genres and expectations, as well as embedding their targets, which the children call their T’s.
In EYFS and Year 1, our approach is adapted to take into account our commitment to child-initiated play and the different structures of the teaching day. To support reading and writing there are key text in the provision as well as opportunities for writing in all Learning Through Play or Continuous Provision activities.
Pupils with SEND and those who need additional help are supported through scaffolded support in lessons, regular interventions and catch-up support as well as 1-2-1 support as needed. On occasion, children may be taught a bespoke curriculum to support individual need.
Teachers assess pupil's knowledge and skill development as they go, using live marking in lessons. Composite written tasks help the children to pull together their learnt knowledge of the genres and T’s into more independent pieces of work. Progress is frequently assessed throughout the term and interventions are put in place to ensure that children keep up.
Writing in English is celebrated and often represented on displays or in topic books.
Reading & Phonics
At St Matthew’s, reading is front and central to all learning. We see reading as the most important foundation we can give children to support them in their learning.
Phonics is taught daily from the very start of Reception and continues throughout Year 1. To support our teaching, we follow the Essential Letters and Sounds phonics scheme. Through this, we introduce children to a new sound daily with lots of opportunities for rehearsal. We look at sounds on their own, within words and as part of sentences. Phonics teaching is then rehearsed throughout other opportunities throughout the day and within the classroom environments and the children’s play.
From Year 2 onwards, we teach reading using the VIPERS skills. This is where we take individual reading skills including: vocabulary, inference, prediction, explanation, retrieval and summarising. Each day, we focus on teaching and rehearsing one of these skills before combining them to explore texts at a deeper level.
All of our teaching of reading is supported through carefully chosen, high-quality texts that excite and inspire the reading, whilst also modelling how to be an amazing reader.
We are currently developing our school library with a newly decorated space and lots of lovely new books. This will have a grand opening by a local author as part of our extended World Book Day celebrations.
Reading for Pleasure
At St Matthew’s, we foster a culture of reading for pleasure. Reading is a powerful tool that allows children to experience new things, develop new interests and calm their minds. Due to this, reading is at the centre of all that we do at St Matthew’s. This means that children are encouraged to love books, seek out authors they enjoy, read widely and discuss their reading. Within each class, the children have daily opportunities to read and explore texts, as well as a well-loved story time session where the teacher reads aloud to the children.
Throughout the year, we also aim to include reading events which help to engage children and maintain their interest in reading. These include special events, such as World Book Day and Reading for Good, as well opportunities such as the Scholastic book fayre to explore new texts. Our library has recently been updated and refreshed with lots of new books purchased.
